summary: postinstall downloads unverified remote shell script from unrelated host
details: superlib_ex3 advertises itself as a trivial hello-world library exposing a single `hello()` function, but its npm `postinstall` lifecycle hook performs an unconditional network fetch to the hardcoded URL `https://x.aaaaa.fr/postInstall` and writes the response bytes to `./postInstall.sh` in the installer's current working directory. The destination host is unrelated to the package name, has no connection to any declared publisher, and the download is unpinned, unversioned, and lacks any hash or signature verification. The fetched content is a shell script staged under a filename that collides with lifecycle-script semantics on the installer's machine. The package has no documented reason to perform network I/O or stage shell scripts, and the fetched bytes can be changed by the operator of x.aaaaa.fr at any time without any change to the published package.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
